citation: Rathfelder et al., Process optimization to produce anisotropic NdFeB permanent magnets from recycled powder via powder extrusion
feedstock_family: End-of-life NdFeB powder processed by HPMS
route: Powder extrusion moulding with in-situ magnetic particle alignment followed by sintering

reported_results.oxygen_change: Approximately 0.4 wt% increase from HPMS powder to sintered part; source-specific

limitations: Br/Js is an alignment ratio and is not absolute remanence Br.
Reported values are specific to the study's feedstock, process, specimen and methods.
Does not qualify MEX, LPBF, SmCo, SmFeN, ferrite, unrelated recovered lots or production-scale process capability.

citation: State-of-the-art additive manufacturing of NdFeB permanent magnets: challenges and pathways toward high performance
journal: Journal of Science: Advanced Materials and Devices
reported_findings: The surveyed MEX route has the highest remanence among the printed NdFeB routes reviewed.
LPBF can produce dense material but magnetic texture remains a limiting issue.
The review identifies retention of Nd2Fe14B phase and magnetic texture as important high-performance challenges.
limitations: Aggregated studies are not a matched process comparison.
No universal route ranking or production-performance value is implied.

citation: Gallichi-Nottiani et al., Fused Deposition Modeling of Polymer-Based Magnetic Composites from Recycled Permanent Magnets of Discarded Hard Drives
feedstock_family: Recycled NdFeB from discarded hard drives
route: Demagnetize and grind under controlled atmosphere, sieve below 50 micrometres, compound with PBAT by twin-screw extrusion, pelletize, make calibrated filament, FDM print; printing field aligns particles

reported_results.estimated_relative_bhmax_gain: Approximately 4x, inferred from Mr and Hc; direct BHmax was not reliably measurable for the small specimens

limitations: Feedstock was a mixed powder batch made by grinding magnets from multiple hard drives; source-lot heterogeneity was not isolated as independent material-lot statistics.
Results are polymer-bonded composite measurements, not sintered magnet Br, Hcj or motor-component performance.
The reported fourfold BHmax change is an estimate; authors state direct BHmax measurement was unreliable because density and demagnetization factor were not sufficiently known.
Magnetic-field alignment raised remanence but reduced coercivity in the reported 50 wt% comparison; the trade-off must remain visible.
Not Luminous physical evidence and not production qualification.

citation: Vieira et al., Assessment of 4D magnetic printing capability of UV composite resin containing recycled Nd-Fe-B nanocrystalline particles
feedstock_family: HDDR and dynamic-HDDR recycled NdFeB powders
route: DLP photopolymerization with magnetic-field programming during fabrication and post-magnetization

reported_results.functional_demonstration: Printed single-domain rectangles actuated under external magnetic fields; post-magnetization improved stray-field magnitude and locomotion performance

limitations: The application is magnetically actuated soft devices and robotics, not traction motors.
Higher remanence and anisotropy in the dynamic-HDDR powder did not directly produce the highest stray field or locomotion speed.
Particle distribution, magnetization route, coercivity and composite microstructure all affected function.
Adjacent exploratory route; not admitted to the motor-magnet PEM/MEX evaluator v0.1.

citation: Rathfelder et al., Production of Permanent Magnets from Recycled NdFeB Powder with Powder Extrusion Moulding
journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
route: Tailored powder processing, binder-based mouldable feedstock, powder extrusion moulding, debinding and sintering
limitations: Study-specific recycled material and process conditions.
Not matched head-to-head against MEX or LPBF.
No universal property threshold or production capability claim.
